user.description:
After adding the device, press its button within 10 minutes. It pairs through any of your proxies within range. If the 10 minutes pass, press the device's *Start pairing* button in Home Assistant first.

A second-hand device must be factory reset first: hold its button for 10 seconds.

unknown_device.message: Device {device_id} is not a ConnectSensors sensor on a loaded network.

value_out_of_range.message: The value does not fit a {kind} reading.

already_paired.message: {name} is already paired. To pair it again, remove it and add it with its pairing code.

device_unreachable.description:
Home Assistant has not heard from {name} since {last_seen}: three heartbeat intervals of {heartbeat} minutes, and 5 minutes more. Its readings show as unavailable until it is heard again.

Check its battery and that a proxy within range is online. If the device's heartbeat is set to something other than {heartbeat} minutes, change it in the device's settings.
device_unreachable.title: {name} is unreachable

pairing_stalled.description:
{name} keeps repeating its pairing request although Home Assistant answered it. It was probably paired with another server, or Home Assistant was restored from an older backup.

Hold the device's button for 10 seconds to factory-reset it, then press it again. If that does not help, move the device closer to a proxy.
pairing_stalled.title: Pairing {name} stalled

proxy_mismatch.description:
{name} uses {proxy_settings}, but the network uses {network_settings}. Home Assistant sends no downlinks through it, so devices only it hears cannot pair or get their acknowledgements.

Set `region: {region}` in the proxy's ESPHome configuration and install it again. This issue clears when the proxy reports matching settings.
proxy_mismatch.title: Proxy {name} uses other radio settings

re_pair.title: Re-pair {name}: press its button near one of your proxies

confirm.title: Re-pair {name}
confirm.description:
This version of the integration uses new frame tags and a new pairing procedure. {name} lost its pairing when its firmware was updated for them, so Home Assistant no longer hears it, and its readings show as unavailable.

Press the device's button once, near one of your proxies, within 10 minutes of opening this repair. When the device's *Pairing* sensor shows *Paired*, submit this form.

If pairing does not finish, hold the button for 10 seconds to factory-reset the device, then press it again.

error.not_paired: {name} is not paired yet. Press its button near one of your proxies, wait a few seconds, and submit again.

abort.not_loaded: The ConnectSensors network is not loaded.

To give {name} a key of its own, paste this into its ESPHome configuration and install it:

```yaml
{snippet}```

When you submit, Home Assistant replaces the old key, and {name} is offline until it connects with this one.

single_path.description:
For more than a day, only {proxy} has heard {name}. If that proxy goes offline, Home Assistant loses the device.

Add a proxy within range of {name} to give it a second path. This issue clears once another proxy hears it.
single_path.title: Only one proxy hears {name}

mailbox_unreachable.title: Mailbox server {url} is unreachable
mailbox_unreachable.description:
Home Assistant has not been connected to the mailbox server {url} for over an hour. The last error was: {error}.

While it is unreachable, devices heard only through neighbours are not received, and neighbours cannot use your proxies through it. Check the address in the federation options, and that the server is running. This issue clears when Home Assistant connects again.

mailbox_refused.title: Mailbox server {url} refused this home
mailbox_refused.description:
The mailbox server {url} refused Home Assistant ({code}). With NOT_PERMITTED, the server only admits its members: ask its operator to admit this home, or remove the server in the federation options. With BAD_PROOF, the server rejected the proofs for your devices' tags, which should not happen with a correct server.

This issue clears when the server accepts the home again.

single_path_federated.title: {name} is heard only through neighbours
single_path_federated.description:
For more than a day, {name} has reached Home Assistant only through neighbours' proxies. If they go offline, or stop sharing their coverage, Home Assistant loses the device.

Add a proxy of your own within range of {name}. This issue clears once two of your own proxies hear it.

init.title: Federation
init.description:
Federation lets homes help each other through mailbox servers. Your sensors can reach Home Assistant through a neighbour's proxies, and your proxies can carry a neighbour's sensors. Readings stay encrypted: neither the mailbox server nor the neighbour can read them.

Pairing is never federated. A new device is always paired near one of your own proxies; afterwards it can be moved anywhere a neighbour's proxy hears it.

Everything here is off until you turn it on.

data.federation_downlinks: Let neighbours' sensors use my proxies to receive replies
data.ignore_federated_events: Ignore events heard only through neighbours
data.ignore_federated_readings: Ignore readings heard only through neighbours

data_description.mailbox_servers: The wss:// address of each mailbox server to use. Home Assistant keeps a separate key for each one.
data_description.federation_owner: Your sensors' frames heard by neighbours' proxies are delivered to you, and Home Assistant can answer them through those proxies. A device heard only this way gets queued commands with its next confirmed uplink, which can take up to its heartbeat interval.
data_description.federation_publish: Frames your proxies hear that belong to none of your devices are passed to the mailbox servers, which deliver them only to their owners. Pairing requests are never passed on.
data_description.federation_downlinks: Neighbours can ask your proxies to transmit the replies to their sensors' frames that your proxies heard. Your own devices come first, and neighbours get at most 0.5% of each proxy's airtime. Needs *Share my coverage with neighbours*: neighbours can only ask about frames you shared.
data_description.ignore_federated_events: A neighbour's proxy or a mailbox server that is a device's only path controls when its frames arrive. Turn this on to fire no events, such as button presses, from frames that came only through federation.
data_description.ignore_federated_readings: The same for readings: keep the last value instead of one that came only through federation.
data_description.mailbox_certificate: Only for a mailbox server with a self-signed certificate: paste its certificate (PEM) to trust it, in addition to the usual certificate authorities.
